items.abstract: <jats:p>Training agentic large language models (LLMs) for complex, multi-step tasks is critically hindered by exploration collapse and inefficient data use. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Automated Multi-agent Trajectory Evolution System (AutoMATES), an evolutionary framework that establishes a self-improving data flywheel. Unlike passive experience replay, AutoMATES actively bootstraps high-quality training data through a closed loop of multi-path adversarial trajectory generation, learned critic-based selection, and domainaware trajectory evolution. This loop continuously produces, refines, and exploits diverse, highperformance action sequences. Our key contributions include: (1) an evolutionary training paradigm that reformulates policy optimization as trajectory evolution; (2) an adversarial generation strategy to enhance exploration; and (3) a domain-specialized mutation mechanism. Extensive evaluations on ALF-World, WebShop, and AIME (2024/2025) benchmarks show that AutoMATES achieves new stateof-the-art results. For example, on ALFWorld, it raises the success rate from 72.8% to 97.2% for a 1.5B model. Ablations confirm the necessity of all components, with the evolution step being the most critical. AutoMATES also generalizes well to a visionlanguage task (Sokoban), attaining an 89.4% success rate. These findings demonstrate that proactively evolving trajectories-rather than merely replaying them-offers a robust and scalable framework for training competent agentic LLMs.</jats:p>
title: STRIVE: Self-Improving Agent Training via Evolutionary Trajectory Flywheel

items.abstract: <jats:p>AI-agent evidence packages are meant to make agent actions independently checkable after the original runtime or provider API is unavailable. This short communication asks when accepting an authentic evidence package also means accepting a fresh action. We model an Agent Evidence Package style flow in Tamarin with agent authorization, gateway forwarding, signer issuance, timestamping, ledger anchoring, and verifier acceptance. The model verifies authentication, integrity, timestamp-event linkage, conditional non-repudiation, forward-integrity-style attribution, and corrupt-gateway boundary properties under explicit assumptions. It also falsifies stateless replay uniqueness: the same valid package can be accepted twice without signature forgery or payload tampering. A replay-cache variant restores uniqueness while preserving an executable honest flow. The result separates authenticity from fresh-action semantics and motivates explicit verifier profiles for reusable agent evidence objects.</jats:p>
title: Freshness Is Not Authenticity: Symbolic Replay Semantics for Agent Evidence Packages
